quote.mainText: There will, of course, be a lot of interesting things, but you won't hear everything, because two concerts or operas will be held in different theaters and halls in one evening.
quote.sourceText: Letter from Boris Lyatoshynsky to Margarita Tsarevich, 29 September 1957, Berlin

title-with-quote.quoteText: It is quite useless for you <...> to try to persuade me that I should not attach so much weight to my troubles and failures, and to assure me of your confidence in the vitality of my works. Let us not dispute this matter: neither view can be proved. What truly matters here is my own conviction—one that, of course, brings me no comfort—that the contrary is the case. The years will pass, and we—that is, the greater part of today’s composers—will survive only in encyclopedic dictionaries, and even then, not all of us. In the end, the question will not be for us to resolve. It will be visible there, but to whom?
title-with-quote.sourceText: Letter from Borys Lyatoshynsky to Lev Chetvertakov, July 22, 1965, Kyiv

title-with-quote.title: LIaTosHynSKy's ArTiStRy
title-with-quote.quoteText: Oh, my dear, my dear darling, when will that time finally come when we will be together, in the living room, where it's so beautiful, there's a piano and lots of sheet music.
title-with-quote.sourceText: Letter from Borys Liatoshynsky to Margarita Tsarevych, May 4, 1916, Saratov
